paragraphs: Here's what I take from this one, friend. God told Ezekiel to dig through a wall, haul out his bags and eat his bread shaking, and all of it was one message: what I say is coming, is coming. The people had eyes to see and ears to hear, but they didn't, because they were "a rebellious house" (Ezekiel 12:2). God wasn't hiding anything from them. He showed it to them right out in the open, as they watched.

Then look at what the people told themselves. They had a proverb, "The days go by, and every vision fails," and they said Ezekiel's vision was for many years from now (Ezekiel 12:22, 27). I think that's the most human thing in the whole passage. When God's word hasn't shown up yet, waiting starts to sound like it's never coming, and I'll be honest, I've talked myself into that on a slow day. But God answers with "None of My words will be delayed any longer. The message I speak will be fulfilled, declares the Lord GOD" (Ezekiel 12:28).

So what do we do with that, baker? We take God at His word, and we take it seriously the first time He says it. Every promise He makes is as good as done, and every warning is just as real. That's why I keep my ovens ready for the Marriage Supper (Revelation 19:9), and since no one knows the day or the hour (Matthew 24:36), I'd rather be caught with a warm oven than a cold one.
